tickets.summary: Deluge system’s north-quadrant isolation valve was closed and unrecorded, leaving coverage potentially unavailable until reopened; duration unknown. This safety-critical protection limits fire escalation, and recurring nozzle blockage may further reduce coverage.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The deluge branch had a confirmed loss of function because its isolation valve was chained closed, with unknown duration and no impairment control to prevent recurrence. The engineer also reports recurring marine-growth and scale blockage that can leave coverage ineffective even when the skid appears healthy; the valve was reopened, but the absence of a status record leaves near-term reliability uncertain.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this isolation valve can remove deluge coverage for the north quadrant of the wellhead area, degrading a safety-critical fire protection layer and allowing a hydrocarbon fire to escalate into a major accident. No redundancy is identified, although the impact is limited to the affected branch rather than the entire deluge system; the unknown period of closure also means the protection impairment could have remained hidden.

urgency.rationale: Today: the deluge branch was found chained closed, leaving a safety-critical fire-protection layer defeated for the north quadrant, and no impairment was recorded. Although the valve was reopened immediately, the unknown duration of closure and absent register entry mean the protection-layer impairment was undeclared when discovered.

tickets.recommended_action: Today, record the deluge impairment and unknown closure duration in the deviation register, then function-test the north-quadrant branch and clear any blocked nozzles; close the action only when the valve is tagged open and full design coverage is demonstrated.
tickets.review_reason: Every ticket is approved by a human before it enters the work queue. Urgency was set by the protection layer override. The equipment is a Safety Critical Element.

tickets.summary: Damp, stained insulation and rust beneath cladding affect the separator vessel shell at the manway; it remains hidden until insulation removal. As the pressure boundary for the first stage, it protects against loss of containment; concealed wall loss or weeping remain possible.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Damp insulation, staining, and rust running from beneath the cladding indicate an active, unquantified corrosion-under-insulation mechanism that cannot be assessed visually because the wall is concealed. The thick wall, historically trouble-free service, and reliability prior of 8 reduce the near-term failure likelihood, but there is no thickness measurement or evidence that the corrosion has plateaued.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this unreplicated first-stage production separator could rupture the pressure boundary, causing a major hydrocarbon release with fire/explosion and escalation consequences; it is a Safety Critical Element protecting against that major-accident scenario. The damp, stained insulation only indicates possible concealed wall loss or cracking rather than confirming its extent, but no redundancy is available to reduce the consequence.

urgency.rationale: Today: the finding indicates active, unquantified corrosion under insulation on the pressure boundary of a non-redundant Safety Critical Element, and concealed wall loss cannot be ruled out without removing the cladding. The extent of damage is uncertain, so this is immediate integrity assessment rather than the top score for a confirmed defeated barrier.

tickets.recommended_action: Today, make the first-stage separator safe for access, remove cladding and wet insulation around the manway, then complete visual and UT thickness checks for corrosion, cracking or weeping; close out with integrity-engineer acceptance or a defined repair.
tickets.review_reason: Every ticket is approved by a human before it enters the work queue. The equipment is a Safety Critical Element.
